reviews.text: Como Treinar o Seu Dragão tem uma vibe deliciosa do início dos anos 2000 que simplesmente conforta o meu coração, (mesmo sendo eu uma gen alpha). A animação não tem a resolução perfeita dos filmes ultra modernos de hoje, mas essa estética com carinha de antiga é justamente o que dá todo o charme e deixa a experiência tão quentinha e sessão da tarde. A história do Soluço com o Banguela é fofa demais e constrói uma amizade muito genuína, dá vontade de ter um dragão de estimação (ou um gatinho preto dos olhos verdes). É uma animação gostosa de ver num dia preguiçoso só pelo quentinho na alma que ela traz.

I really enjoyed How to Train Your Dragon. The story was fun, emotional, and had some beautiful animation. The friendship between Hiccup and Toothless was easily my favorite part of the movie, and it made the adventure even more enjoyable. The action scenes were exciting, and the movie had a good balance of humor and heartfelt moments. Overall, it's a great animated movie that I would happily watch again.

i have no qualms with the premise that humans have been mistreating a species for centuries because they assumed its hostility. in fact, i like it, and i find it particularly creative for a kids movie. where this film goes wrong for me is the characterization. Hiccup’s father is the classic, obstinate parent who shows no affection for his son until Hiccup saves the vikings’ lives. This characterization irks me because at that point his father is just hopping on the bandwagon. It’s like cheering for the Yankees- ok, cool, you support something obviously supportable. the character arc only works if his father shows him affection prior to him proving himself, which doesn’t occur. Astrid doesn’t work for me either, because she is giving no backstory. I have no idea why she has an all consuming thirst to kill dragons, she just comes off as rude to Hiccup for no reason but blind competitiveness. however, as my dad pointed out, this movie is going to make for a great ride at universal

Haven't rewatched this in a bit. Never really loved it, the film's humor is that grating DreamWorks animation humor that I've come to associate with bad animated movies so that doesn't help. I also don't think the animation is aging particularly well, there's a dead eyed stare that I kept noticing in all the characters that was not flattering. This is definitely a movie that connected with a ton of people and I think there's even an argument for a queer reading of it but it just doesn't quite get to the point where it gets me invested in it.

I LOVED this book in primary school, but the movie coming out when I was hitting puberty was exactly the wrong time for me to give a shit about it. Better late than never. Watching it now, I don't remember the book being such a generic hero's journey template. Just the basic synopsis and knowing it's Dreamworks is enough to predict the whole thing beat by beat with zero surprises. Not a fair criticism for a kids movie perhaps, but knowing how fresh and original the source material was I'm very underwhelmed. For an original IP I'd have been more lenient. Disliked the voice acting a lot, Hiccup's actor especially... so nasal and obviously a grown ass adult putting on a kid's voice. Very strange mix of Scottish and American accents to portray the Vikings. Why not get, I dunno, the Skarsgard family to do some hammy Scandinavian accents instead? Not a fan of the dragon designs either, way too cartoony. Straight out of Rayman. Even for a kids movie they could have been scarier and more realistic to raise the stakes a bit. The music was banging though, I'll give it that. The test drive scene choked me up so some magic is certainly there, but it's too by-the-numbers for me overall.

Alors bon, c'est dynamique, plutôt rigolo et assez court, mais de là à mettre plus de 3 étoiles, quand même pas!

En fin de compte, je crois que c'est un film qu'on a beaucoup trop mis sur un piédestal alors qu'il faut être honnête et se l'avouer...c'est pas si ouf. Alors oui, c'est divertissant. Les 1h30 passe à une vitesse folle, tout est fait pour que tu passes un bon moment devant. L'esthétique est efficace, le montage s'arrête jamais de bout en bout. Et puis, vu que c'est des dragons....................je pense qu'on y est tous très sensibles, c'est sûrement la créature fantastique la plus fantasmé et ce pour une raison : les dragons, c'est cool. L'oeuvre réussit à nous investir émotionnellement, clairement. On est prit par les personnages, on se prend d'affection pour certains, on se met à en détester d'autres,...donc je dirais que ça marche bien. Enfin, les designs dans leur ensemble sont bien foutus, que ce soit au niveau des dragons comme des personnages, tout fonctionne. Donc, ça parait être vraiment bien ce que je raconte, alors pourquoi je l'adore pas ? Parce que c'est un film basique. Et je suis désolé hein, mais tout fonctionne, sans que rien ne soit nouveau. Dans tout les points forts que j'ai émis, tout est ok, tout marche, sans vraiment réussir non plus. Et c'est là que pour moi le film a été un échec, c'est qu'il n'a jamais réussit à me surprendre, à m'étonner. Il est simple, straightforward et ne cherche jamais à nous donner plus que ce qu'on à déjà reçu. Ça répond simplement à nos attentes, sans aller plus loin. Que ce soit visuellement ou narrativement, ça reste très plat. Les couleurs sont sympas sans sortir de l'ordinaire, le travail sur les lumières, pareil et l'histoire va droit au but, avec un dynamisme presqu'un peu trop prononcé. Alors oui, c'est un bon script, oui l'animation est très bien, mais moi ça ne me suffit pas pour y voir un grand film d'animation américain. Selon moi, ça reste une oeuvre qui fait pale figure à côté d'un Chat Potté 2 par exemple. Ça c'est un grand film d'animation américain qui pousse son concept, qui impressionne en mêlant 3D et 2D, utilisant des petits moments de musique hyper intense mais qui sait aussi utiliser son drame avec un message beau et puissant. Y'a des moments plus lent, stressant, bref c'est un vrai roller coaster qui ne se laisse pas emporter par son scénario mais qui comprend les enjeux de l'oeuvre. Ça, c'est fort, ça c'est beau. Bref, c'était mignon, sympa, j'ai passé un bon moment, mais j'y vois pas un grand film.
